![](data:image/png;base64,)

Evidence and explanation / หลักฐานและคำอธิบาย:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Compose reads variables from .env.example and interpolates them into compose.yml before starting the containers. For example, values such as \${POSTGRES_DB}, \${POSTGRES_USER}, and \${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} are filled in from the environment file. These are interpolation variables at Compose time. In addition, the services declare explicit runtime variables inside the environment: block, such as PORT, PGHOST, PGDATABASE, and PGUSER. Those are the variables the container actually receives at runtime. In other words, .env supplies values to Compose, while environment: tells containers what to run with.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The staging and production shapes were previewed with config only. This is enough to compare how the overlays change ports, services, and networking without starting three active stacks. The point is to inspect the merged Compose result, not to leave multiple live deployments running at once. This avoids port conflicts and keeps the local experiment clean.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Request path / เส้นทางคำขอ:

Laptop browser → NPM container (gacha.test:80, forward app:3000) → app container (:3000) → db container (db:5432)

| Item                             | Direct local                                                           | Local proxy                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Browser URL                      | <http://localhost:8085/test>                                           | <http://gacha.test/backend/test>                                                                   |
| Host entry port                  | 8085 published by compose.local.yml (127.0.0.1:8085 → app:3000)        | 80 published by the npm service (gacha.test resolves to 127.0.0.1); the app publishes no host port |
| App service/internal port        | 3000 (container port 3000, published as 8085 on the host)              | 3000, reached only as app:3000 inside gacha-6788185_default; no host port                          |
| Database volume name             | gacha-6788185_pgdata                                                   | gacha-6788185_pgdata (same volume, reused — not recreated)                                         |
| Original history ID + created_at | draw id 1 (transaction 3), Wind Fox / COMMON, 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z | unchanged: draw id 1, Wind Fox / COMMON, 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z                                  |

Evidence and explanation / หลักฐานและคำอธิบาย:

1. **02 — Route through local NPM / ส่งคำขอผ่าน NPM ในเครื่อง**

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

The proxy topology used three files only: compose.yml (base), compose.production.yml (adds restart: unless-stopped to app and db) and compose.proxy.yml (adds the npm service). compose.local.yml was left out deliberately, so the 127.0.0.1:8085:3000 mapping is gone: the app service in the base file declares no ports at all, and only NPM publishes host ports — 80:80, 443:443 and the admin UI bound to 127.0.0.1:81. The app and the database are therefore reachable only inside the project network, which is why docker compose ps lists npm as the single entry point while app shows no published port.

**Task 02-1: Open NPM admin at <http://127.0.0.1:81>; complete the initial administrator setup shown by your version.**

Initialize nginx:

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

Before login:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

After:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

app and npm join the same project default network, gacha-6788185_default, where Compose registers each service name as a DNS alias. That shared network is why the NPM proxy host can use the upstream app:3000 — the service name and the internal port, never a host port. Inside the npm container, localhost (or 127.0.0.1) means the NPM container itself: every container has its own loopback interface, so localhost:3000 from NPM asks for a process inside the NPM image, where nothing listens on 3000, and the proxy would answer 502. Docker's embedded DNS resolves app to the app container's IP on the shared network instead.

**Task 02-2: Add 127.0.0.1 gacha.test to your laptop's hosts file, preserving existing entries.**

Adding host:  
![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Task 02-3: Create a Proxy Host for gacha.test, scheme http, forward hostname app, port 3000. Use local HTTP for this .test name.**

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

**Task 02-4: Add a Custom Location /backend/, also forwarding to http, app, 3000. In that location's gear/advanced field put only:**

rewrite ^/backend/(.\*)\$ /\$1 break;

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The Proxy Host for gacha.test forwards http to app:3000, and its Custom Location /backend/ forwards to the same upstream with only the advanced rewrite rewrite ^/backend/(.\*)\$ /\$1 break;. NPM generates the surrounding location block and proxy_pass itself, so pasting another location or a second proxy_pass would duplicate them. Because the prefix is stripped, /backend/test reaches the app as /test, and the test page derives its API prefix from its own URL, so every button calls /backend/api/... and is rewritten to /api/... . Health, wallet, recharge, exchange, draw and history all answered 200/201 through the proxy, so the logic buttons work behind the prefix as well.

**Task 02-5: Save and open <http://gacha.test/backend/test>. Check that health and all logic buttons work. The proxy sends /backend/test to the app as /test; its API buttons must also pass through /backend/.**

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

The local stack was stopped with docker compose down, without -v, so Docker removed the containers and the project network but kept the named volume. STUDENT_ID stayed 6788185, so the project name gacha-6788185 — and with it the volume gacha-6788185_pgdata — was unchanged when the production + proxy stack started. The history row that this volume already held was read back through the proxy, unchanged and never re-inserted: draw id 1, Wind Fox / COMMON, created_at 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z. The button test in step 8 added new transactions and draw id 2 (River Sprite), but it did not replace or modify row 1. Only the app container and the request path changed; the database storage did not.

**Task 02-6: Retrieve the history row saved in experiment 01 without drawing a replacement. Confirm the database volume identity is unchanged.**

The saved history still returns the original row: id 1, Wind Fox, created_at 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z — read back through the proxy, not re-inserted. The River Sprite draw created by the button test sits above it as a separate newer row (id 2), and no stored row was replaced. The database volume gacha-6788185_pgdata is the same one the stack started with.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Task 02-7: Draw the path: laptop browser → NPM container → app:3000 → db:5432. Explain why localhost inside NPM means NPM itself, not the separate app container.**

Because each container has its own loopback, that means 127.0.0.1 never leaves its container. Inside NPM container, nothing listens to :3000, so the :3000 just points to NPM itself.
